accuracy.evidence: Matches A level Mathematics content 'understand and use simple, discrete probability distributions' and CCSS S-MD.1, 3 and 4. The two-dice total gives P(X=x)=(6-|x-7|)/36, P(X≤4)=6/36, P(X<4)=3/36, P(X≥10)=6/36; kx over 1 to 4 gives k=0.1; the larger score gives (2y-1)/36. All values were checked by counting the 36 cells.

misconceptions.evidence: Addresses the standard errors: totals assumed equally likely (1/11 for seven, prediction and challenge 'equal'), k=1/n instead of using the sum (k slider, 'share' tag), ≤ confused with < ('incl' and shading buttons), negative probabilities accepted ('neg', sorter), and relative frequency read as the exact probability (roll step, 'exact'/'est').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpdist builds a bar chart live from taps on a 6 by 6 outcome grid, a k slider with a running sum of kx, a draggable inequality cut that shades cumulative bars, a 10/100/1000 roll simulation over a dashed model, and a second variable built from the same grid. The existing flagprob lab only treats single-event fractions; shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners see why seven is most likely because its six cells light together, see 10k climb to exactly 1 on the slider, watch the shaded bars change when the cut switches between ≤ and <, and see relative-frequency bars wobble at 10 rolls and settle near the model at 1000, which makes the theory-versus-data distinction concrete.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions: the most likely total of two dice, the value of k when P(X=x)=kx for x=1 to 4, whether 1000 rolls match the model exactly or only closely, and P(Y=6) for the larger score before its distribution is built. Each is checked by the interaction that follows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with ten tags (share, flip, equal, value, over, neg, incl, single, exact, est). Wrong answers name the slip, for example that 6/36 is P(X ≤ 4) not P(X < 4), or that a list summing to 1 is still invalid with a negative entry.

readability.evidence: Learner audience: kid text FK 4.2 against the 6.5 target and adult text FK 8.6 against 9.5, measured by the validator. Notation is defined before use: capital X as the random variable, small x as a value, P(X = x), cumulative P(X ≤ x), sample space and relative frequency.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean and overlap under 12 percent. Kid paragraphs move from random variable, to counting outcomes, to the sum-to-1 rule with the kx example, to inequalities and data; adult paragraphs give the specification wording, key terms, five named mistakes and the lab sequence.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light for all six steps: the 6 by 6 grid sits above the bar chart, axis labels and fractions on bars stay readable, the slider spans the width, and the ≤ < ≥ > buttons wrap in rows. walk.cjs passes on desktop and iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe finds no AA violations in either theme. Every gesture has a button route: Build P(X = 2) steps through totals, k ± 0.01 and Check Σ = 1, sign buttons and Cut ← → for the inequality, Roll 10/100/1000 and Reset; the canvas aria-label and live text read each probability as a fraction.
